# API index (generated by tools/api-index.mjs — do not edit by hand)

Header comment + export signatures of every shared module. Open the file itself only when you need the implementation.

## js/core/dom.js

```
DOM helpers: a safe `html` template tag (everything interpolated is escaped unless it is itself
produced by `html`/`raw`), event delegation, form helpers, focus management, <head> meta.

Rule for all UI code: never concatenate data into strings that reach innerHTML; use html`...`.
URLs coming from data must go through safeUrl().
```

```js
export class SafeHtml
export const esc = (v) => String(v ?? '').replace(/[&<>"'`]/g, (c) => ESC[c]);
export const raw = (s) => new SafeHtml(String(s ?? ''));
export function html(strings, ...values)
export const aria = (v) => (v ? 'true' : 'false');
export function render(target, safe)
export function safeUrl(u, fallback = '#')
export const $ = (sel, root = document) => root.querySelector(sel);
export const $$ = (sel, root = document) => [...root.querySelectorAll(sel)];
export function delegate(root, type, selector, handler, opts)
export function bindActions(root, actions = {}, { change = {}, input = {}, submit = {} } = {})
export function readForm(form)
export async function withBusy(btn, fn)
export function debounce(fn, ms = 250)
export const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
export const nextFrame = () => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => r()));
export function focusFirst(container)
export function trapFocus(container)
export function setMeta({ title, description, canonical, image, noindex = false, siteName = 'Shop Verse', type = 'website', jsonLd } = {})
export async function copyText(text)
export function downloadFile(name, content, type = 'text/plain;charset=utf-8')
```

## js/core/errors.js

```
Error handling: turn SDK / rules / network failures into plain, actionable messages.
Nothing is ever swallowed silently, and nothing is reported to a remote service (there is none):
errors go to the console and, for the admin panel, to an in-memory ring buffer shown in Setup.
```

```js
export class AppError extends Error
export function explainError(err, fallbackKey = 'err.generic')
export const isRefusal = (e) => !!e && (e.name === 'AppError' || e.name === 'OrderBuildError');
export const isPermissionDenied = (e) => /permission-denied|insufficient permissions/i.test(`${e?.code} ${e?.message}`);
export const isNetworkError = (e) => /unavailable|network|offline|deadline/i.test(`${e?.code} ${e?.message}`);
export function reportError(err, context = '')
export const recentErrors = () => ring.slice().reverse();
export function installGlobalErrorHandlers(show)
export const langIsBn = () => getLang() === 'bn';
```

## js/core/firebase.js

## js/core/format.js

```
Formatting: money (৳ with lakh grouping), numbers, dates in Bangladesh time, relative time.
Digits can be switched to Bengali numerals (settings.ui.banglaDigits / user toggle) without
touching any call site: everything goes through these helpers.
```

```js
export function setFormatOptions({ banglaDigits, language } = {})
export const getFormatOptions = () => ({ banglaDigits: bnDigits, language: lang });
export const toBnDigits = (s) => String(s).replace(/[0-9]/g, (d) => BN[d]);
export const toLatinDigits = (s) => String(s).replace(/[০-৯]/g, (d) => String(BN.indexOf(d)));
export function groupLakh(n)
export function num(n, { decimals = 0 } = {})
export function money(n, { sign = false } = {})
export const pct = (n) => digits(`${Math.round(Number(n) || 0)}%`);
export function compact(n)
export function fmtDate(v, { month = 'short' } = {})
export function fmtTime(v)
export function fmtDateTime(v)
export function fmtShortDate(v)
export function fmtMonth(v)
export function dhakaDayKey(ms)
export function startOfDhakaDay(ms)
export function parseDhakaDate(str, endOfDay = false)
export function toDhakaInput(ms)
export function fromDhakaInput(str)
export function relTime(v, nowMs = Date.now())
export const plural = (n, one, other) => (Number(n) === 1 ? one : other);
export const initials = (name) => String(name || '?').trim().split(/\s+/).slice(0, 2).map((w) => [...w][0] || '').join('').toUpperCase() || '?';
export const truncate = (s, n = 80) => { const str = String(s ?? ''); return str.length > n ? str.slice(0, n - 1).trimEnd() + '…' : str; };
export function fileSize(bytes)
export function fmtPhone(p) { const s = String(p || ''); return /^01\d{9}$/.test(s) ? `${s.slice(0, 5)}-${s.slice(5)}` : s; }
export const maskPhone = (p) => { const s = String(p || ''); return s.length >= 6 ? `${s.slice(0, 3)}${'•'.repeat(s.length - 5)}${s.slice(-2)}` : s; };
export const maskEmail = (e) => { const [u, d] = String(e || '').split('@'); return d ? `${u.slice(0, 2)}${'•'.repeat(Math.max(1, u.length - 2))}@${d}` : String(e || '');
```

## js/core/i18n.js

```
Tiny i18n layer (English + Bengali).

  registerStrings('bn', { 'cart.title': 'আপনার কার্ট' });     // any module can add strings
  t('cart.title')                                              // current language → English → key
  t('cart.items', { n: 3 })                                    // "{n}" interpolation
  tn('cart.items', 3)                                          // picks cart.items_one / cart.items_other
  lbl(ORDER_STATUS.pending)                                    // picks .bn / .label from a constants entry

Default language is Bengali (the store's customers); the choice is remembered in localStorage.
Pages keep their own strings next to their code (registerStrings at module top level) so
parallel work never collides on one big dictionary.
```

```js
export function registerStrings(language, strings)
export function registerBoth(pairs)
export function initI18n({ key = 'sv.lang', fallback = 'bn' } = {})
export const getLang = () => lang;
export function setLang(next)
export function onLangChange(fn) { listeners.add(fn); return () => listeners.delete(fn); }
export function t(key, params, fallback)
export function has(key) { return key in dict[lang] || key in dict.en; }
export function tn(key, n, params = {})
export function lbl(entry, fallback = '')
export const pick = (en, bn) => (lang === 'bn' ? bn : en);
```

## js/core/invoice.js

```
Printable invoice — shared by the customer's order page and the admin order page.

  invoiceHtml(order, store)    SafeHtml for one normalised order (shared/orderModel.normalizeOrder)
                               store = settings(): { name, logoUrl, contact: { phone, email, address } }

The sheet is appended to <body> only while printing; css/pages/invoice.css hides everything else (@media print).
```

## js/core/print.js

```
Printable documents: invoice, packing slip, shipping label — shared by the admin panel (orders) and the
customer's account page (invoice of their own order).

  printDocument(invoiceHtml(order, { business }), { title: 'Invoice SV-…' })      // opens the print dialog
  const doc = invoiceHtml(order, { business, lang: 'en' })                          // SafeHtml, e.g. to preview in a modal
  const business = businessFrom(settings(), privateSettingsOrNull)

`order` is the output of normalizeOrder() (works for legacy orders too).
Printing happens inside a hidden iframe (srcdoc) with its own small stylesheet, so it never depends on the
page's CSS and nothing from the app chrome leaks onto the paper.
```

## js/core/pwa.js

```
Service worker registration, update prompt and install prompt.
  initPwa({ onUpdate(apply) })   – onUpdate gets a function that activates the waiting worker
  canInstall() / promptInstall() / onInstallAvailable(fn)
The worker itself is /sw.js: pages network-only (offline page on failure), same-origin code/images network-first; Firebase/Firestore/Auth traffic is never touched.
Used by the storefront and the admin panel.
```

```js
export const canInstall = () => !!deferredPrompt;
export function onInstallAvailable(fn) { installListeners.add(fn); if (deferredPrompt) fn(true); return () => installListeners.delete(fn); }
export async function promptInstall()
export function initPwa({ onUpdate } = {})
```

## js/core/router.js

```
Router (History API for the storefront, hash routes for /admin/).

Page module contract (default export of every routed file):

  export default {
    async mount(ctx) { …render into ctx.el…; return () => { …optional cleanup… }; }
  };

ctx = { el, params, query, path, route, router, signal, cleanup(fn) }
  - el       the outlet element (already emptied)
  - params   { slug: 'abc' } from ":slug" segments, `rest` for "*rest"
  - query    plain object from the query string
  - signal   AbortSignal that aborts when the user navigates away (check before touching the DOM after await)
  - cleanup  register teardown callbacks (listeners, onSnapshot unsubscribes …)

Route table entries: { path: '/product/:slug', load: () => import('./pages/product.js'), meta?: {…} }
`guard({route, params, query, path})` may return a path string to redirect to (auth / permission checks).
```

```js
export function parseQuery(search)
export function buildQuery(obj = {})
export function createRouter({ mode = 'history', base = '', routes, outlet, guard, notFound, onChange, announcer } = {})
```

## js/core/theme.js

```
Light / dark / system theme. The choice is stored per app (storefront and admin keep separate keys)
and applied as <html data-theme="light|dark">; "system" removes the attribute so the
prefers-color-scheme media query in tokens.css decides. js/theme-init.js applies the stored
value before first paint to avoid a flash.
```

```js
export function effectiveTheme()
export const getTheme = (key) => { const v = local.get(key, 'system'); return MODES.includes(v) ? v : 'system'; };
export function initTheme(key)
export function setTheme(key, mode) { const m = MODES.includes(mode) ? mode : 'system'; local.set(key, m); apply(m); return m; }
export function cycleTheme(key) { const cur = getTheme(key); return setTheme(key, MODES[(MODES.indexOf(cur) + 1) % MODES.length]); }
export function toggleTheme(key) { return setTheme(key, effectiveTheme() === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'); }
```

## js/core/validate.js

```
Form validation. Validators return an error *message* (already translated) or '' when valid.

  const { ok, errors, values } = validateForm(readForm(form), {
    name:  [required, minLen(2)],
    phone: [required, phone],
  });
  showFormErrors(form, errors);            // sets aria-invalid + fills #err-<name>

Mirrors the constraints in firestore.rules so people see the problem before the server rejects the write.
```

```js
export const required = (v) => (blank(v) ? t('v.required') : '');
export const minLen = (n) => (v) => (blank(v) || String(v).trim().length >= n ? '' : t('v.min', { n }));
export const maxLen = (n) => (v) => (blank(v) || String(v).length <= n ? '' : t('v.max', { n }));
export const phone = (v) => (blank(v) || normalizePhone(v) ? '' : t('v.phone'));
export const email = (v) => (blank(v) || PATTERNS.email.test(String(v).trim()) ? '' : t('v.email'));
export const slug = (v) => (blank(v) || PATTERNS.slug.test(String(v)) ? '' : t('v.slug'));
export const integer = (v) => (blank(v) || Number.isInteger(Number(v)) ? '' : t('v.int'));
export const minValue = (n) => (v) => (blank(v) || Number(v) >= n ? '' : t('v.minValue', { n }));
export const maxValue = (n) => (v) => (blank(v) || Number(v) <= n ? '' : t('v.maxValue', { n }));
export const url = (v) =>
export const trxId = (v) => (blank(v) || PATTERNS.trxId.test(String(v).toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g, '')) ? '' : t('v.trx'));
export const password = (v) => (blank(v) || String(v).length >= 8 ? '' : t('v.password'));
export const matches = (other) => (v, all) => (v === all[other] ? '' : t('v.match'));
export const custom = (fn) => fn;
export function validateForm(values, schema)
export function showFormErrors(form, errors = {})
export function clearFormErrors(form) { showFormErrors(form, {}); }
export { focusFirst };
```

## js/data/account.js

```
The signed-in customer's own data: address book and notifications.
(Profile fields are handled by data/auth.js → saveProfile; wishlist / cart by their own modules.)

  await listAddresses(uid)                      → [{ id, label, name, phone, district, upazila, area, postalCode, line1, isDefault }]   default first
  await saveAddress(uid, input, id?)            → id            (creates or replaces; first address becomes the default)
  await deleteAddress(uid, id)                  (promotes another address to default when the default was deleted)
  await setDefaultAddress(uid, id)
  validateAddress(input)                        → { name?: msg, phone?: msg, district?: msg, line1?: msg }   ({} = valid)
  normalizeAddressInput(input)                  → clean object (phone normalised to 01XXXXXXXXX)

  const off = watchNotifications(uid, (list) => …, onError)    newest first, max 50 → [{ id, title, body, kind, orderNumber, ticketId, read, createdMs }]
  await markNotificationRead(uid, id) / markAllNotificationsRead(uid, ids) / deleteNotification(uid, id)

Every write follows firestore.rules (users/{uid}/addresses, users/{uid}.defaultAddressId, notifications.read).
```

```js

export function normalizeAddressInput(a = {})
export function validateAddress(input = {})
export async function listAddresses(uid)
export async function saveAddress(uid, input, id = null)
export async function setDefaultAddress(uid, id)
export async function deleteAddress(uid, id)
```

## js/data/auth.js

```
Authentication + the signed-in person's profile and staff role.

  await initAuth();                       // once, at start-up
  const s = getAuthState();               // { ready, user, profile, staff }
  onAuthChange((s) => …)                  // fires immediately when ready, then on every change
  can('orders.update')                    // UI gating only — firestore.rules are the real enforcement
  actor()                                 // { uid, email, role } for the order/inventory planners

Staff roles live in staff/{uid} (writable only by Super Admin through the rules). A person with no
staff document is a customer. The profile document users/{uid} is created on first sign-in.
```

## js/data/cart.js

```
Shopping cart — local-first, synced to users/{uid}/cart/main for signed-in customers.

The cart stores only line keys and quantities (+ the unit price seen when the item was added, so
the UI can say "price changed"). Names, images and prices always come from the catalog;
the authoritative price is re-read from the inventory document at checkout and re-checked by
the security rules when the order is written.

  cart.add(key, qty)          → throws AppError('too_many_lines') beyond MAX_LINES distinct items
  cart.setQty(key, n) / cart.remove(key) / cart.clear()
  cart.subscribe(fn)          → fn(lines) on every change; returns unsubscribe
  resolveCart(catalog, lines) → display lines with state: ok | out | limited | removed
```

```js
export const cart =
export function bindCartToAuth(onAuthChange)
export function resolveCart(catalog, cartLines = lines, nowMs = Date.now())
export function unitKeyFor(product, chosen) { return findUnit(product, chosen)?.key || null; }
```

## js/data/catalog.js

```
Storefront catalog: categories, brands, published products and their inventory, loaded in bulk
(the catalog is small) so search, filtering and sorting are instant and run in the browser.

Caching
  - meta/catalog holds a version stamp bumped by every staff catalog write. Content (categories,
    brands, products) is cached in localStorage and reused while the stamp is unchanged.
  - Inventory (price / stock / reserved) changes with every order, so it is cached for only 2 minutes
    and ALWAYS re-read from Firestore at cart / checkout time (refreshInventory).

  const cat = await loadCatalog();            // { products: ProductView[], categories, brands, inv, … }
  queryProducts(cat, { q, categoryId, brandId, min, max, onSale, inStock, sort })
  productBySlug(cat, slug), productById(cat, id), relatedProducts(cat, p, 8)

ProductView is the shape returned by shared/productModel.normalizeProduct().
```

```js
export async function loadCatalog({ force = false } = {})
export const getCatalog = () => mem;
export function invalidateCatalog() { mem = null; local.remove(STORAGE_KEYS.catalog); local.remove(KEY_INV); }
export async function refreshInventory(keys)
export const productById = (cat, id) => cat?.byId.get(id) || null;
export const productBySlug = (cat, slug) => cat?.bySlug.get(slug) || null;
export const categoryBySlug = (cat, slug) => cat?.categories.find((c) => c.slug === slug) || null;
export const brandBySlug = (cat, slug) => cat?.brands.find((b) => b.slug === slug) || null;
export function categoryPath(cat, categoryId)
export const SORTS = ['relevance', 'newest', 'popular', 'rating', 'price_asc', 'price_desc', 'name'];
export function queryProducts(cat, o = {})
export function suggestProducts(cat, q, limit = 6) { return cat ? runSuggest(cat.products, q, limit) : []; }
export function priceBounds(products)
export function relatedProducts(cat, product, n = 8)
export const newestProducts = (cat, n = 8) => queryProducts(cat, { sort: 'newest' }).slice(0, n);
export const bestSellers = (cat, n = 8) => queryProducts(cat, { sort: 'popular' }).filter((p) => p.soldCount > 0).slice(0, n);
export const saleProducts = (cat, n = 8) => queryProducts(cat, { onSale: true, sort: 'popular' }).slice(0, n);
export const featuredProducts = (cat, n = 8) => queryProducts(cat, { featured: true }).slice(0, n);
export function recentlyViewed() { return local.get(STORAGE_KEYS.recent, []); }
```

## js/data/db.js

```
Thin Firestore helpers. Paths are plain strings ('orders/SV-261026-ABC123', 'orders/X/events').

  await getDocData('products/abc')                       → { id, ...data } | null
  await listDocs('orders', { where: [['status','==','pending']], orderBy: [['createdAt','desc']], limit: 25, after: lastSnap })
       → { docs: [{id,...}], last: snapshot|null, size }
  const off = watchDoc('orders/X', (doc|null) => …, onError)
  const off = watchList('orders', opts, (docs) => …, onError)

Timestamps stay Firestore Timestamp objects in memory (shared/pricing.toMillis understands them).
```

```js
export const docRef = (path) => doc(db, ...segs(path));
export const colRef = (path) => collection(db, ...segs(path));
export const snapData = (s) => (s && s.exists() ? { id: s.id, ...s.data() } : null);
export async function getDocData(path) { return snapData(await getDoc(docRef(path))); }
export async function getDocDataSafe(path)
export async function listDocs(colPath, opts = {})
export function watchDoc(path, cb, onError)
export function watchList(colPath, opts, cb, onError)
export function serializeDoc(v)
```

## js/data/orders.js

```
Customer-side order operations.

  quoteOrder({ uid, lines, zone, couponCode })    live totals for the checkout page (fresh inventory + coupon)
  placeOrder({ … })                               builds the atomic write set (shared/orderBuilder) and commits it
  listMyOrders() / getMyOrder(id) / listOrderEvents(id) / watchMyOrder(id, cb)
  cancelMyOrder(order, reason) / requestReturn(order, {lines, reason, details}) / resubmitPayment(order, {trxId, senderNumber})

Prices, stock and coupons are NEVER taken from the cart or the page: every write re-reads the
inventory / coupon documents, and firestore.rules re-derive the same numbers before accepting the batch.
```

## js/data/write.js

```
Commits abstract write operations (js/shared/ops.js) through the Firestore SDK.

Atomicity matters: a status change and its stock effect, or an order and its inventory
reservation, MUST land in one batch (the security rules bind them together with getAfter()).
  commitAtomic(ops)            – exactly one batch; throws if it cannot be atomic
  commitChunked(ops, {size})   – bulk jobs (imports, migrations); each chunk atomic, the job idempotent
```

```js
export function toSdk(value)
export async function commitAtomic(ops)
export async function commitChunked(ops, { size = LIMITS.ADMIN_BATCH_OPS, onProgress } = {})
export const setDocData = (path, data, merge = false) => commitAtomic([{ op: 'set', path, data, merge }]);
export const updateDocData = (path, data) => commitAtomic([{ op: 'update', path, data }]);
export const deleteDocData = (path) => commitAtomic([{ op: 'delete', path }]);
```

## js/shared/auditView.js

```
Audit log viewer — the pure part (no DOM, no Firebase), so it can be tested without a browser.

The log (`auditLogs`) is written by the planners next to every staff action: who (uid, e-mail, role), what (action code + a one-line summary),
on what (entity + id) and the before/after values. It is read with ONE ordering (newest first) and an optional lower time bound — both use the
automatic single-field index, so the project needs no composite index. Everything else (search, area, person) filters what is loaded.

  sinceFor(period)                 the time bound of a period chip (null = everything)
  normalizeEntry(id, doc)          a stored document → the plain entry the page works with
  diffEntry(before, after)         what changed, field by field ("status" or "address.district"), as display strings
  entityRoute(entity, id, can)     the admin page an entry is about — only when the viewer may open it
  matchesFilters(entry, filters)   search text / area / person
  tally(entries, key, label)       the values present, most frequent first (for the filter lists)
  rawJson(before, after)           pretty JSON of the two snapshots, capped
```

```js
export const AUDIT = Object.freeze({ PAGE: 100, MAX_LOADED: 1000, VALUE_MAX: 300, DEPTH: 3, FIELDS_MAX: 60, RAW_MAX: 20000 });
export const PERIODS = Object.freeze(['24h', '7d', '30d', 'all']);
export const isPeriod = (p) => PERIODS.includes(p);
export const sinceFor = (period, nowMs = Date.now()) => (SPAN[period] ? nowMs - SPAN[period] : null);
export function normalizeEntry(id, d = {})
export function showValue(v, max = AUDIT.VALUE_MAX)
export function flatten(value, depth = AUDIT.DEPTH, prefix = '', out = [])
export function diffEntry(before, after)
export function rawJson(before, after)
export function entityRoute(entity, id, can = () => true)
export function matchesFilters(e, { q = '', entity = '', actor = '' } = {})
export function tally(entries, key, labelOf = (e) => e[key])
```

## js/shared/contentFlow.js

```
Content — pure planners (no I/O) for the home page layout and the CMS pages, so the admin pages and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  homeProblems(sections)                           → [[en, bn], …]   everything that must stop a save: validateHome() plus pictures and links that the
                                                                     storefront would silently drop (an editor must never "save" something that then vanishes)
  planHomeSave({ sections, before, actor })        → { ok, action, ops, sections } | { ok:false, error, problems? }        (forbidden · invalid · no_change)
  planPageSave({ page, existing, isNew, actor })   → { ok, id, action, ops } | { ok:false, error, errors? }               (forbidden · invalid · exists · not_found · no_change)
  planPageFlag({ page, field, value, actor })      → { ok, id, action, ops }     field: 'visible' | 'footer'               (forbidden · not_found · invalid · no_change)
  planPageDelete({ page, actor })                  → { ok, id, action, ops }                                                (forbidden · not_found)
  homeSummary(sections) · pageSummary(page)

firestore.rules lets everyone with content.write (Super Admin, Store Admin, Product Manager) write content/home and pages/{slug}; pages must have a clean slug,
only the known fields, sizes within limits and the server time. The storefront sanitises both on every read (contentModel.normalizeHome / normalizePage /
markdown), so nothing written here can break a customer's screen.
  • the home layout is saved as the SANITISED sections (normalizeHome) — what is stored is exactly what visitors get
  • every change is audited: content.home_save · page.create · page.update · page.show · page.hide · page.footer_on · page.footer_off · page.delete
    (the audit entry records titles and sizes, never the page text)
  • saving what is already stored is refused (no_change), so the audit log holds only real changes; the slug of a page never changes (create a new page instead)
```

```js
export const CONTENT = Object.freeze({ PERM: 'content.write', RESERVED_SLUGS: Object.freeze(['new']) });
export const PAGE_FLAGS = Object.freeze(['visible', 'footer']);
export function homeSummary(sections = [])
export function pageSummary(p = {})
export function homeProblems(sections)
export function planHomeSave({ sections, before = null, actor })
export function planPageSave({ page, existing = null, isNew = false, actor })
export function planPageFlag({ page, field, value, actor })
export function planPageDelete({ page, actor })
export { LIMITS_HOME, PAGE_LIMITS, PAGE_SLUG_RE };
```

## js/shared/couponFlow.js

```
Coupons — pure planners (no I/O), so the Coupons page and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  normalizeCode(text)                                                → 'EID-2026'  (trimmed, upper-case)
  validateCouponForm(form, { creating, current, catalog, nowMs })    → { ok, code, values, errors }       errors: { field: code }
  planCouponSave({ creating, form, current, catalog, actor, nowMs })  → { ok, code, values, action, ops } | { ok:false, error, errors? }
  planCouponActive({ code, active, current, actor })                  → { ok, code, action, ops } | { ok:false, error }
  planCouponRemove({ code, current, actor })                          → { ok, code, ops } | { ok:false, error }
  couponStatus(coupon, nowMs)                                         → 'live' | 'scheduled' | 'expired' | 'exhausted' | 'disabled'
  describeOffer(coupon)                                               → '10% off, max 200'  (English, for the audit log)

firestore.rules lets `coupons.write` (Super Admin, Store Admin) write coupons/<CODE> without looking at its shape, but the ORDER rule
trusts the stored coupon (type, value, maxDiscount, minOrder, dates, customerIds, scope) when it re-derives a discount — so a coupon
with a wrong shape is a price list with a bug. This file is the validator:
  code ^[A-Z0-9-]{3,24}$ and never changes · type percent | fixed | free_shipping · percent 1–100 (optional cap) · fixed whole taka
  minOrder ≥ 0 · endsAt after startsAt (and in the future for a new coupon) · usageLimit ≥ what was used already · scope all |
  categories | products (ids must exist) · customerIds = the only accounts that may use it (empty = everyone)
Staff never write usedCount / lastOrderId / createdAt (checkout does, through the rules). A coupon that has been used cannot be deleted:
switch it off instead, the history stays. Every change is one atomic batch: the coupon + one audit entry.
```

```js

export const COUPON_LIMITS = Object.freeze({ amountMax: 1000000, minOrderMax: 10000000, usageMax: 1000000, perCustomerMax: 1000, descMax: 200, productsMax: 100, categorie
export const CODE_PATTERN = /^[A-Z0-9-]{3,24}$/;
export const normalizeCode = (text) => String(text ?? '').trim().toUpperCase();
export function couponStatus(c, nowMs = Date.now())
export function describeOffer(c)
```

## js/shared/customerFlow.js

```
Customers — pure planners (no I/O), so the admin pages and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  planRestrict({ customer, reason, actor })               → { ok, id, action, ops } | { ok:false, error, errors? }
       error codes: forbidden · not_found · self · no_change · invalid (errors.reason: required · too_short · too_long)
  planUnrestrict({ customer, actor })                     → same shape        (forbidden · not_found · no_change)
  planNoteAdd({ customer, text, count, actor, noteId })   → { ok, id, noteId, action, ops }     (forbidden · not_found · invalid (errors.text: required · too_long) · too_many)
  planNoteDelete({ customer, note, actor })               → { ok, id, noteId, action, ops }     (forbidden · not_found)
  planSubscriberRemove({ subscriber, actor })             → { ok, id, action, ops }             (forbidden · not_found)
  planExport({ kind, count, actor })                      → { ok, action, ops }   one audit entry for a bulk CSV export   (forbidden · invalid)
  summarizeCustomerOrders(orders)  → { orders, completed, cancelled, spent, average, firstMs, lastMs }
  filterCustomers(list, { q, status }) · orderCustomers(list) · lookupKind(q) · filterSubscribers(list, q)

`customer` is a view from customerModel.normalizeCustomer, `note` from normalizeNote, `subscriber` from normalizeSubscriber.

firestore.rules lets everyone with customers.write (Super Admin, Store Admin) change ONLY restricted / restrictedReason / restrictedAt / updatedAt on a
customer and refuses a restriction that has no reason of 3–200 characters or a restrictedAt that is not the server time. What the restriction does:
the customer's checkout is refused (the rules' order gate). Nothing else about the account changes.
  • every change is audited: customer.restrict / customer.unrestrict / customer.note_add / customer.note_delete / newsletter.remove / customer.export / newsletter.export
  • the audit entry of a note records that a note was written (and its length), never its words — notes may hold private details
  • a bulk export of personal data needs BOTH customers.read and reports.export (Super Admin and Store Admin) and is itself audited
  • nobody restricts their own account; internal notes are one document each (userPrivate/{uid}/notes/{id}) so two people never overwrite each other
```

```js
export const CUSTOMER = Object.freeze(
export const EXPORT_KINDS = Object.freeze(['customers', 'subscribers']);
export function planRestrict({ customer, reason = '', actor })
export function planUnrestrict({ customer, actor })
export function planNoteAdd({ customer, text = '', count = 0, actor, noteId })
export function planNoteDelete({ customer, note, actor })
export function planSubscriberRemove({ subscriber, actor })
export function planExport({ kind, count = 0, actor })
export function summarizeCustomerOrders(orders = [])
export function filterCustomers(list, { q = '', status = '' } = {})
export const orderCustomers = (list) => (list || []).slice().sort((a, b) => (b.joinedMs || 0) - (a.joinedMs || 0) || String(a.id).localeCompare(String(b.id)));
export function lookupKind(q)
export function filterSubscribers(list, q = '')
```

## js/shared/inventoryFlow.js

```
Manual stock changes — pure planners (no I/O), so the browser and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  planStockChange({ key, inv, mode: 'add'|'remove'|'set', qty, reason, note, actor, nowMs })
      → { ok, key, before, after, delta, ops }  |  { ok:false, error }
      one atomic batch: the inventory document, one immutable stock movement, the catalog stamp and an audit entry
  parseStockCsv(text)                    → { ok, rows:[{line, ref, count}] } | { ok:false, error }
  planStockImport({ rows, units, actor, nowMs })
      → { ok, items:[{line, ref, key, sku, name, before, after, delta, status: change|same|error, error}], chunks:[ops[]], changes, same, errors }
  planReservationFix({ orders, invByKey, actor, nowMs })   → { ok, diffs, chunks }

"add" and "remove" use an increment (a concurrent change by someone else is kept); "set" (a stock count) writes the counted number itself.
A CSV import is a stock count, so every changed unit is written as an absolute number: running a chunk twice gives the same stock.
Each chunk of an import or recount is its own atomic batch (≤ 18 operations); a failed run is repeated from a fresh preview.
```

## js/shared/migration.js

```
Legacy → v2 migration planner (pure; the admin "Setup & migration" page executes the ops).

Principles
 - Non-destructive: legacy fields (image, oldPrice, desc, stock …) are left in place; new fields are ADDED.
 - Idempotent: running it twice produces no duplicate work. Products that already have status+type are skipped.
 - Honest: nothing is invented. Stock quantities did not exist in the legacy data, so "In Stock" products
   become *untracked* (no limit) until someone enters counts, and "Out of Stock" products become tracked with 0.
 - Every written document must pass firestore.rules for a Super Admin (tests/rules/migration.rules.test.mjs).
```

## js/shared/ops.js

```
Abstract write operations.

Business logic (orderBuilder, orderFlow, inventory planners …) never talks to Firestore directly.
It returns a list of plain operations:

  { op: 'set' | 'update' | 'delete', path: 'orders/SV-261026-ABC123', data: {...}, merge?: true }

`data` may contain three sentinels (plain objects, so they survive JSON and tests):
  TS        → server timestamp          (Firestore serverTimestamp())
  inc(n)    → numeric increment         (Firestore increment(n))
  DEL       → delete this field         (Firestore deleteField())

js/data/write.js turns these into SDK calls; tests/rules/harness.mjs turns them into the rules
engine's own representation. Keeping this layer pure lets the exact same code run in the browser
and in the rules tests.
```

```js
export const TS = Object.freeze({ $op: 'ts' });
export const DEL = Object.freeze({ $op: 'del' });
export const inc = (n) => ({ $op: 'inc', n });
export const isSentinel = (v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && typeof v.$op === 'string';
export function chunkOps(ops, size = 18)
export function clean(value)
```

## js/shared/orderBuilder.js

```
Builds the complete, atomic write set for placing an order.

The write set is exactly what firestore.rules expects (see the header of that file):
  - one `inventory/{lineKey}` update per line (reserve stock + bind it to this order),
  - optional coupon counter + per-customer usage record,
  - optional `paymentTrx/{TRXID}` uniqueness record (manual bKash / Nagad),
  - `users/{uid}.lastOrderAt` stamp (cooldown / restricted-account gate),
  - the order document itself, with prices and totals re-derived from the inventory documents.

Pure function: no I/O. Used by js/data/orders.js (browser) and by the rules tests.
```

```js
export class OrderBuildError extends Error
export function buildOrder(i)
export { lineEligible };
```

## js/shared/orderFlow.js

```
Order lifecycle planners.

Each planX() function is pure: it takes the current order (normalizeOrder() shape), the actor
and fresh inventory documents, validates the request against the lifecycle rules and returns
  { ok: true, ops: [...], summary }  or  { ok: false, error: '<code>', message }
The ops are abstract writes (see ops.js) that are committed in ONE batch, so a status change, its
stock effect, the customer-visible timeline entry, the customer notification and the audit entry
either all happen or none do.

Stock model
  • placing an order      → inventory.reserved += qty            (done by orderBuilder)
  • Shipped / Delivered   → stock -= qty, reserved -= qty        (physical deduction, once)
  • Cancelled (pre-ship)  → reserved -= qty                      (reservation released)
  • Returned + restock    → stock += qty
"Physical deduction happened" is derived from order.shippedAtMs, so it can never run twice.
```

## js/shared/productFlow.js

```
Staff-side product planners (pure: no I/O, the same code runs in the browser and in the rules tests).

  cleanProductForm(raw)                  → normalised form (trimmed text, integer money, bounded lists)
  validateProductForm(form)              → { ok, errors: { field: code }, variantErrors: { index: { field: code } } }
  planProductSave({ mode, id, form, existing, unique, actor, nowMs, names })
       → { ok, pre, core, ops, id, slug } | { ok:false, error, errors?, variantErrors? }
       pre  = inventory documents, SKU index, stock movements: idempotent, committed in chunks of ≤ 18 BEFORE the core
       core = the product document, slugIndex, productPrivate, catalog stamp and audit entry: ONE atomic batch (≤ 8 ops)
  planProductStatus({ products, status, actor, nowMs })      bulk publish / unpublish / archive → { ok, chunks, skipped }
  planProductDelete({ id, existing, actor, nowMs })          refuses while stock is reserved by open orders (archive instead)

Rules these mirror (firestore.rules validProduct): name 1–200, slug pattern ≤ 120, status draft|published|archived, type simple|variable,
integer price 0–1e8, salePrice null or below price, ≤ 90 keys. Existing inventory documents are never given a new `stock` here:
stock of an existing unit changes only through the inventory page (which writes a movement), so a product edit cannot overwrite
units that customers reserved in the meantime.
```

## js/shared/reportFlow.js

```
Reports — the rules of the game, pure (no Firebase, no DOM), so the page, the data layer and the tests run the very same code.

  resolveRange({ preset, from, to, nowMs })    → { ok, preset, fromMs, toMs, days, fromKey, toKey } | { ok:false, error, field }
       presets: today · 7d · 30d · month · lastMonth · custom (from / to are Bangladesh dates "YYYY-MM-DD", at most 366 days)
       error codes: invalid (field: preset · from · to) · order · too_long
  previousRange(range)                         → the period of the same length right before it (the "vs previous period" comparison)
  pickUnit(days) · groupBuckets(daily, unit)   → hour (one day) · day (≤ 62 days) · week (≤ 186) · month — what one bar of the sales chart is
  compare(current, previous)                   → { delta, pct }   pct is null when there is nothing to compare with
  buildReport({ orders, prevOrders, range, categoryNames }) → every number the Reports page shows
  exportSheet(kind, { orders, range, withCustomer })        → { filename, headers, rows }    kinds: orders · daily · products
  planReportExport({ kind, count, range, actor })           → { ok, action, ops } | { ok:false, error }    (forbidden · invalid · empty)

Definitions (the page repeats them, nobody has to guess what a number means — see also shared/stats.js):
  sales      = order totals of orders in a revenue status (confirmed … delivered); pending, cancelled, returned and refunded orders do not count
  orders     = every order placed in the period, whatever its status
  received   = the part of sales whose payment is verified or collected
  customers  = different signed-in customers who placed an order in the period (counted from the orders themselves — no extra data is read)
  cancel rate = cancelled orders / all orders placed, in percent
Days are Bangladesh days (UTC+6, no daylight saving). A comparison always uses the period of equal length that ends the moment this one starts.

Personal data: a sheet carries the customer's name and phone only when `withCustomer` is set (the caller passes customers.read). A bulk export is itself audited
(one `report.export` entry with the sheet's kind, its row count and the period — never the rows) and needs reports.read AND reports.export.
```

```js
export const REPORT = Object.freeze({ READ: 'reports.read', EXPORT: 'reports.export', MAX_DAYS: 366, TOP: 10, TOP_SMALL: 8 });
export const PRESETS = Object.freeze(['today', '7d', '30d', 'month', 'lastMonth', 'custom']);
export const EXPORT_KINDS = Object.freeze(['orders', 'daily', 'products']);
export const dayKey = (ms) => { const d = new Date(ms + DHAKA_OFFSET_MS); return `${d.getUTCFullYear()}-${pad(d.getUTCMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getUTCDate())}`; };
export const timeKey = (ms) => { const d = new Date(ms + DHAKA_OFFSET_MS); return `${dayKey(ms)} ${pad(d.getUTCHours())}:${pad(d.getUTCMinutes())}`; };
export function dayFromKey(key)
export function resolveRange({ preset = '30d', from = '', to = '', nowMs = Date.now() } = {})
export function previousRange(range)
export const pickUnit = (days) => (days <= 1 ? 'hour' : days <= 62 ? 'day' : days <= 186 ? 'week' : 'month');
export function groupBuckets(daily, unit)
export function compare(current, previous)
export function buildReport({ orders = [], prevOrders = [], range, categoryNames = {} } = {})
export function exportSheet(kind, { orders = [], range, withCustomer = false } = {})
export function planReportExport({ kind, count = 0, range, actor })
```

## js/shared/reviewFlow.js

```
Review moderation — pure planners (no I/O), so the admin Reviews page and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  planReviewModeration({ review, to, note, approved, approvedCapped, productRating, productExists, productName, reportIds, actor, nowMs })
       → { ok, id, action, ops, followUp, rating, reportsCleared } | { ok:false, error, errors? }
       to: 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'pending'       (error codes: forbidden · not_found · bad_status · no_change · invalid)
  planReviewDelete({ review, approved, approvedCapped, productRating, productExists, productName, reportIds, actor, nowMs })   → same shape
  planReportsDismiss({ review, reportIds, productName, actor })      → { ok, id, action, ops, followUp }      (error: no_reports)
  nextRating({ review, wasApproved, willBeApproved, approved, approvedCapped, productRating })   → { ratingSum, ratingCount, ratingAvg }
  groupReports(reports)                                  → Map reviewId → [{ id, reason, createdMs }]   newest first
  filterReviews(list, { q, rating, verified, names })    → list          orderReviews(list, status) → sorted copy

`review` is a view from reviewModel.normalizeReview. `approved` is the FRESH list [{ id, rating }] of the product's approved reviews,
`reportIds` the document ids of the reports filed against the review (reviewReports/{reviewId__reporterUid}).

firestore.rules lets everyone with reviews.moderate (Super Admin, Store Admin, Product Manager, Customer Support) change a review in any way and
change ONLY ratingSum / ratingCount / ratingAvg on a product. So this file is what keeps the numbers honest:
  • a review counts towards the product's rating only while it is APPROVED. Every change in or out of "approved" (approve, reject, back to pending,
    delete) rewrites the three rating fields from the fresh list of approved reviews — self-healing: a wrong number is repaired the next time any
    review of that product is moderated. When the product has more approved reviews than one read can return (`approvedCapped`), the stored
    aggregate is adjusted instead.
  • moderation stamps the review (moderatedBy, moderatedAt, moderationNote = the reason of a rejection, shown to the author) and never touches
    what the customer wrote; a rejection / deletion also clears the reports filed against the review (they are answered)
  • any change that rewrites the rating also bumps meta/catalog so shops that cached the catalog fetch the new stars
  • every change is audited: review.approve / review.reject / review.pending / review.delete / review.reports_dismiss
Reports beyond what fits in the first atomic batch go to `followUp` (committed in chunks afterwards; a failure there only leaves reports behind).
```

```js

export function nextRating({ review, wasApproved, willBeApproved, approved = [], approvedCapped = false, productRating = null })
export function planReviewModeration(
export function planReviewDelete(
export function planReportsDismiss({ review, reportIds = [], productName = '', actor })
export function groupReports(reports = [])
export function filterReviews(list, { q = '', rating = 0, verified = '', names = {} } = {})
export function orderReviews(list, status)
```

## js/shared/reviewModel.js

```
Product reviews — pure helpers shared by the storefront and the admin moderation page.

  reviews/{PRODUCTID__UID}   one review per customer per product (the document id enforces it)
    { productId, userId, userName, rating 1–5, title, text, status: pending|approved|rejected,
      verified, orderNumber, lineKey, helpfulCount, createdAt, updatedAt,
      moderatedBy, moderatedAt, moderationNote   ← added by a moderator (shared/reviewFlow.js); never by the customer }

`verified` is only ever true for a delivered order that contains the product — the security rules read that order
(`orders/{orderNumber}.items[lineKey].productId`), so a customer cannot claim it for something they did not buy.
The shapes below mirror the field lists and length limits in firestore.rules; the rules stay the authority.

  validateReview(input)            → { rating?, title?, text? }   codes: required | short | long   ({} = valid)
  buildReviewDoc({...})            → document for the first write (status 'pending')
  findVerifiedLine(orders, pid)    → { orderNumber, lineKey } | null     (newest delivered, non-legacy order)
  summarize(reviews)               → { count, avg, dist: [n1..n5] }
  ratingFields(approvedReviews)    → { ratingSum, ratingCount, ratingAvg }  (what moderators write back to the product)
```

## js/shared/shippingFlow.js

```
Shipping zones — pure planners (no I/O), so the Shipping page and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  validateZoneForm(form, { zones, id, fallbackActive })   → { ok, values, errors, overlap }      errors: { field: code }
  planZoneSave({ creating, id, form, zones, actor })      → { ok, id, values, action, ops } | { ok:false, error, errors?, overlap? }
  planZoneActive({ id, active, zones, actor })            → { ok, id, action, ops, uncovered } | { ok:false, error, overlap? }
  planZoneRemove({ id, zones, actor })                    → { ok, id, ops } | { ok:false, error }
  coverage(zones)                                         → { total, covered, uncovered[], byDivision[], owner: Map(district → zone) }
  exclusiveDistricts(zones, id)                           → districts that ONLY this active zone covers (what a switch-off would uncover)
  overlaps(zones, id, districts)                          → [{ district, zoneId, zoneName }] already held by another ACTIVE zone

firestore.rules lets anyone holding `shipping.write` write shippingZones/<id> without looking at its shape — this file is the validator:
  name 1–60, unique · districts: known districts, at least one · fee: whole taka 0–5000 · freeOver: empty or whole taka 1–1,000,000
  etaMin ≤ etaMax: whole days 0–60 · a district belongs to ONE active zone (checkout picks the zone by district; two active zones would
  make the price depend on list order). A switched-off zone may keep any districts.
The orders rule re-reads the zone (active, districts, name, fee, freeOver) for every order, so a change made here IS the price list.
The zone id is the slug of its first name and never changes (past orders keep the name they were placed under).
Every change is one atomic batch: the zone + one audit entry. Only a switched-off zone can be deleted.
```

```js
export function planZoneActive({ id, active, zones = [], actor })
```

## js/shared/staffFlow.js

```
Staff & roles — pure planners (no I/O), so the Staff page and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  validateStaffForm(form, { creating })     → { ok, values, errors }          errors: { field: code }
  planStaffSave({ creating, uid, form, current, staff, actor })
      → { ok, uid, values, action, ops }  |  { ok:false, error, errors? }
  planStaffRemove({ uid, current, staff, actor })   → { ok, ops } | { ok:false, error }
  lastActiveSuperAdmin(staff, uid)          → true when `uid` is the only active Super Admin
  permissionMatrix()                        → [{ group, perms:[{ id, roles:[roleId…] }] }]  (what each role may do, for the reference table)

firestore.rules only requires `staff.manage` (Super Admin) and the shape of staff/<uid>
(role, active, email, name, createdAt, updatedAt, createdBy). The safety nets below live here:
  - nobody changes their own role or switches themselves off (ask another Super Admin)
  - the last active Super Admin can never be demoted, switched off or removed — the panel would lock everybody out
  - only a member who is already switched off can be removed; their history stays in the audit log
Every change is one atomic batch: the staff document + one audit entry.
```

## js/shared/stats.js

```
Sales statistics — pure functions over normalised orders (shared/orderModel.js).
Used by the Dashboard and Reports pages; covered by tests/unit/stats.test.mjs.

Definitions (the UI repeats them, so nobody has to guess what a number means):
  sales      = sum of order totals whose status is in REVENUE_STATUSES (confirmed … delivered).
               Pending, cancelled, returned and refunded orders do not count.
  received   = the part of `sales` whose payment is verified or collected (payment.status === 'paid').
  aov        = sales / number of counted orders (rounded to whole taka).
  orders     = every order placed in the period, whatever its status.

Days are Bangladesh days (UTC+6, no daylight saving), so "today" matches what the shop owner sees on the wall clock.
```

```js
export const DHAKA_OFFSET_MS = 6 * 3600 * 1000;
export const isRevenueOrder = (o) => REVENUE.has(o.status);
export const dayStart = (ms) => Math.floor((ms + DHAKA_OFFSET_MS) / DAY) * DAY - DHAKA_OFFSET_MS;
export const hourStart = (ms) => Math.floor((ms + DHAKA_OFFSET_MS) / HOUR) * HOUR - DHAKA_OFFSET_MS;
export const dhakaHour = (ms) => Math.floor((((ms + DHAKA_OFFSET_MS) % DAY) + DAY) % DAY / HOUR);
export function summarize(orders)
export function buckets(orders, fromMs, toMs, unit = 'day')
export function topProducts(orders, { limit = 5, by = 'revenue' } = {})
export function breakdown(orders, keyFn)
export function categorySales(orders)
```

## js/shared/supportFlow.js

```
Support desk — pure planners (no I/O), so the admin pages and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  planTicketReply({ ticket, text, close, alsoEmail, storeName, actor, nowMs })
       → { ok, id, status, ops, notified, emailed } | { ok:false, error, errors? }
       error codes: forbidden · not_found · invalid (errors.text: required | too_long) · no_mail_permission · no_email
  planTicketStatus({ ticket, to, actor })      → { ok, id, ops }          (bad_status · no_change)
  planTicketPriority({ ticket, to, actor })    → { ok, id, ops }          (bad_priority · no_change)
  filterTickets(list, { q, priority })         orderTickets(list, status) → sorted copy

`ticket` is a view from ticketModel.normalizeTicket. firestore.rules lets everyone with support.reply (Super Admin, Store Admin, Customer Support)
change a ticket in any way and add messages as "staff" — so what is allowed is decided here:
  • a reply is 1–2000 characters (the rules check the same), written under the staff member's own uid, and moves the ticket to "answered"
    (or "closed" when the staff member chose to close it); lastAuthor becomes "staff"
  • a customer with an account is told in-app (users/{uid}/notifications, kind "support", ticketId) — a guest cannot read the ticket back at all,
    which is why a reply can also be queued as an e-mail (mail/{id}, needs mail.send and an address on the ticket)
  • status and priority are changed one at a time; priority never touches updatedAt (it is not customer-visible activity)
  • every action is audited: ticket.reply · ticket.status · ticket.priority (the audit entry never carries the message text)
The ticket document is readable by its customer, so nothing internal is ever written to it.
```

```js
export const SUPPORT = Object.freeze({ PERM: 'support.reply', REPLY_MAX: 2000, PREVIEW_MAX: 140 });
export function planTicketReply({ ticket, text, close = false, alsoEmail = false, storeName = '', actor, nowMs = Date.now() })
export function planTicketStatus({ ticket, to, actor })
export function planTicketPriority({ ticket, to, actor })
export function filterTickets(list, { q = '', priority = '' } = {})
export function orderTickets(list, status)
```

## js/shared/taxonomyFlow.js

```
Categories & brands — pure planners (no I/O), so the admin pages and the rules tests run the exact same code.

  validateTaxonomyForm(kind, form, { items, id })                 → { ok, values, errors }          errors: { field: code }
  planTaxonomySave({ kind, creating, id, form, items, products, actor, nowMs })
                                                                  → { ok, id, values, action, ops, followUp } | { ok:false, error, errors? }
  planTaxonomyVisible({ kind, id, visible, items, actor, nowMs }) → { ok, id, action, ops }
  planTaxonomyRemove({ kind, id, items, refs, actor, nowMs })     → { ok, id, ops, imagePath }     refs = { products, children, coupons[] }
  planCategoryMove({ id, dir: 'up'|'down', items, actor, nowMs }) → { ok, id, action, ops }
  taxonomyCounts(kind, items, products)                           → Map id → { products, children }

kind: 'category' (categories/<id>: name, slug, parentId, image, imagePath, icon, description, sort, visible) or
      'brand'    (brands/<id>:     name, slug, logo, logoPath, description, visible)

firestore.rules only checks WHO may write categories / brands (categories.write / brands.write) and never looks at the shape, so this file
is the validator:  name 1–80 and unique (a category: among its siblings) · slug a–z 0–9 hyphens, unique, made from the name when left empty ·
a category has at most TWO levels (a sub-category cannot have children; a category with children cannot become a sub-category) ·
description ≤ 300 · image: https link or a path on this site (nothing else) · visible on/off.
The id never changes (products point at it); the slug is what the page link is made of and may change.

What a change does to the rest of the catalog:
  • every write also bumps meta/catalog, so shops that cached the catalog fetch it again
  • a new NAME is copied into products (categoryName / brandName) — `followUp` holds those writes (many; committed in chunks after the
    atomic first batch). Saving again repairs anything that did not make it, because stale products are always included.
  • a category or brand that products point at, or a category that has sub-categories, or one a coupon is limited to, cannot be deleted
  • hiding a category hides its sub-categories in the shop too (the shop drops children of a hidden parent)
Every change is audited (category.* / brand.*).
```

```js
export const KINDS = Object.freeze(
export const TAXONOMY_LIMITS = Object.freeze({ nameMax: 80, slugMax: 80, descMax: 300, imageMax: 1000 });
export const SLUG_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/;
export function siblingsOf(kind, items, parentId = null)
export function taxonomyCounts(kind, items, products = [])
export function validateTaxonomyForm(kind, form = {}, { items = [], id = null } = {})
export function planTaxonomySave({ kind, creating = false, id = null, form, items = [], products = [], actor, nowMs = Date.now() })
export function planTaxonomyVisible({ kind, id, visible, items = [], actor, nowMs = Date.now() })
export function planTaxonomyRemove({ kind, id, items = [], refs = {}, actor, nowMs = Date.now() })
export function planCategoryMove({ id, dir, items = [], actor, nowMs = Date.now() })
```

```
Every write re-reads what it changes first, so what is planned is what is stored right now. A refusal is thrown as an AppError with a message for the screen
```

## js/admin/data/inventory.js

```
  await adjustStock({ key, mode, qty, reason, note })     fresh read of the unit → planner → ONE atomic batch

  await applyStockImport(plan, { onProgress })              commits the plan's chunks one after the other → { done, total }

Every change is a batch of its own (≤ 18 operations). An import or recount that stops half-way is simply repeated from a fresh preview:
```

```
A save is not one batch for big variable products (a batch may touch 20 documents): the idempotent part — inventory documents, SKU index,
stock movement — goes first in chunks, then the product document, slug index, cost data, catalog stamp and audit entry land together.
If the second step fails, a repeat of the save completes it; until then the new inventory documents are simply not referenced by any product.
```

```
I/O for the Setup & migration page. The rules of the game live in shared/readiness.js and shared/migration.js.

  await gatherSnapshot()          → the plain snapshot evaluateReadiness() needs (a collection this role may not read is `undefined`)
  await previewMigration()        → the migration plan for the data as it is right now (nothing is written)  — needs migrate.run
  await runMigration(plan, { onProgress })    commits the plan in atomic chunks of 18 operations, in order

The migration is non-destructive and idempotent (see shared/migration.js): an interrupted run is simply started again — it
re-reads the data, finds what is already converted and continues.
```

```js
export async function gatherSnapshot()
export async function previewMigration()
export async function runMigration(plan, { onProgress } = {})
```

## js/admin/data/shipping.js

```
Shipping zones data for the Shipping page. The rules of the game live in shared/shippingFlow.js; this module only does I/O.

  await loadShippingZones()                          → [{ id, name, districts, fee, freeOver, etaMin, etaMax, active, sort }] by sort, then name
  await saveZone({ creating, id, form, zones })      one atomic batch: the zone + an audit entry
  await setZoneActive({ id, active, zones })
  await removeZone({ id, zones })
  overlapText(overlap)                               "Dhaka (Outside Sirajganj), …" in the language of the page

A refusal is thrown as an AppError carrying `.errors` ({ field: message }) when a form field is at fault.
Every write clears the storefront's 5-minute zone cache on this device; other devices pick the change up within 5 minutes.
```

```js
export async function loadShippingZones()
export function overlapText(overlap = [])
export const saveZone = ({ creating = false, id, form, zones }) => commit(planZoneSave({ creating, id, form, zones, actor: actor() }));
export const setZoneActive = ({ id, active, zones }) => commit(planZoneActive({ id, active, zones, actor: actor() }));
export const removeZone = ({ id, zones }) => commit(planZoneRemove({ id, zones, actor: actor() }));
```

## js/admin/data/taxonomy.js

```
Categories & brands data for the admin pages. The rules of the game live in shared/taxonomyFlow.js; this module only does I/O.

  await loadTaxonomy(kind)                → { items, products }   items fresh from Firestore; products = the cached admin catalog, slimmed to what counting needs
  await reloadItems(kind)                 → items                  after a write (the product list does not change by writing a category)
  await saveTaxonomy({ kind, creating, id, form })      one atomic batch (document + audit + stamp), then the product names in chunks
  await setTaxonomyVisible({ kind, id, visible })
  await removeTaxonomy({ kind, id })      refuses while sub-categories, products or a coupon point at it (checked just now, not from the list)
  await moveCategory({ id, dir })
  await uploadTaxonomyImage(kind, file)  → { url, path }           discardUpload(path)  best effort, never throws

kind: 'category' | 'brand'. A refusal is thrown as an AppError carrying `.errors` ({ field: message }) when a form field is at fault.
```

```js
export async function reloadItems(kind)
export async function loadTaxonomy(kind)
export async function saveTaxonomy({ kind, creating = false, id = null, form })
export async function setTaxonomyVisible({ kind, id, visible })
export async function removeTaxonomy({ kind, id })
export async function moveCategory({ id, dir })
export const uploadTaxonomyImage = (kind, file) => uploadSiteImage(kind === 'category' ? 'categories' : 'brands', file, { maxSide: 800, quality: 0.85 });
export const discardUpload = (path) => (path ? deleteStoragePath(path) : Promise.resolve());
```

## js/admin/data/tickets.js

```
Support tickets for the admin pages. The rules of the game live in shared/supportFlow.js; this module only does I/O.

  await loadTicketList(status)           → { items: Ticket[], capped }     'open' | 'answered' | 'closed' — one equality query, at most LIST_CAP
  await loadTicket(id)                   → { ticket, messages } | null     the ticket and its conversation, oldest message first
  await sendReply({ id, text, close, alsoEmail })   the message, the status, the in-app notice, the optional queued e-mail, the audit entry
  await setStatus({ id, to })            await setPriority({ id, to })

Every write re-reads the ticket first, so what is planned is what is stored right now. A refusal is thrown as an AppError with a message for the screen.
```

```js
export const LIST_CAP = 200;
export async function loadTicketList(status)
export async function loadTicket(id)
export async function sendReply({ id, text, close = false, alsoEmail = false })
export async function setStatus({ id, to })
export async function setPriority({ id, to })
```

## js/store/lib/checkoutForm.js

```
Checkout form logic — pure (no DOM, no Firebase), unit-tested in tests/unit/checkout-form.test.mjs.

  normalizeForm(raw)                       → clean copy of every field (trimmed, phone/TrxID normalised)
  validateForm(form, { methods })          → { field: code }   ({} = valid)   codes are mapped to text by the page
  toOrderInput(form, { email })            → { customer, address, payment, note } for data/orders.placeOrder
  addressFromForm(form) / formFromAddress(address, base)

The server side (shared/orderBuilder.js + firestore.rules) re-validates everything; this only gives early, specific feedback.
```

```js
export const METHODS = Object.freeze(['cod', 'bkash', 'nagad']);
export const isMobileMethod = (m) => m === 'bkash' || m === 'nagad';
export function emptyForm(over = {})
export function normalizeForm(raw = {})
export function validateForm(raw, { methods = METHODS } = {})
export function addressFromForm(raw)
export function formFromAddress(a = {}, base = emptyForm())
export function toOrderInput(raw, { email = '' } = {})
```

## js/store/lib/links.js

```
Storefront URL helpers + a tiny handle on the router so any module can navigate without importing app.js.
```

```js
export const setRouter = (r) => { router = r; };
export const getRouter = () => router;
export const go = (path, opts) => { if (router) router.navigate(path, opts); else location.assign(path); };
export const productUrl = (p) => `/product/${enc(p.slug || p.id)}`;
export const categoryUrl = (c) => `/category/${enc(c.slug || c.id)}`;
export const brandUrl = (b) => `/brand/${enc(b.slug || b.id)}`;
export const shopUrl = (query = {}) => `/shop${buildQuery(query)}`;
export const searchUrl = (q) => `/search${buildQuery({ q })}`;
export const orderUrl = (id) => `/account/orders/${enc(id)}`;
export const trackUrl = (id) => (id ? `/track/${enc(id)}` : '/track');
export const pageUrl = (slug) => `/page/${enc(slug)}`;
export const loginUrl = (next) => `/login${next ? buildQuery({ next }) : ''}`;
export const absoluteUrl = (path) => new URL(path, location.origin).href;
export function safeNext(next, fallback = '/')
```

## js/store/components/orderParts.js

```
Shared order view pieces for order-success, the account order page and tracking.
Every function takes a normalised order (shared/orderModel.js → normalizeOrder) and returns SafeHtml.

  methodName(method)             "Cash on Delivery" | "bKash" | "Nagad"
  orderLinesHtml(order, {after}) items: thumbnail, name, variant, qty × price, line total (+ optional extra per line)
  orderTotalsHtml(order)         subtotal / discount / delivery / total
  addressHtml(order)             delivery address block
  paymentHtml(order)             method, payment status, TrxID, sender number
  paymentNote(order)             one plain sentence about what happens with the money next
  stepsHtml(order)               progress: placed → confirmed → processing → shipped → delivered (+ cancelled / return / refund)
  timelineEntries(order, events) merged, oldest-first history (events come from data/orders.listOrderEvents)
  eventsHtml(entries)            the history as a vertical timeline
  orderRowHtml(order, {href})    one <li> in an order list (links to /account/orders/<id> unless href is given)
```

```js
export const methodName = (m) => { const x = PAYMENT_METHODS[m]; return x ? pick(x.label, x.bn) : String(m || ''); };
export function orderLinesHtml(order, { after = null } = {})
export function orderTotalsHtml(order)
export function addressHtml(order)
export function paymentHtml(order)
export function paymentNote(order)
export function stepsHtml(order)
export function timelineEntries(order, events = [])
export function eventsHtml(entries = [])
export function orderRowHtml(o, { href } = {})
```
